chapter_title: [Concerning the Interpretation of] all [the] Fathers of [Light], who are distinguished from one another.
chapter_note: This chapter is largely a catechetical list built on the formula “The beginning of X is Y,” where X often names human virtues/activities (grace, prayer, builders, deliverers). That “X→Y” mapping crosses from cosmos to lived religious/social language and looks like a later didactic application-layer scaffold. Nevertheless, many lines preserve older cosmological identifications/titles of the Fathers of Light and brief functional descriptions (e.g., Living Spirit with five sons; Light Mind as awakener/gatherer). The opening attribution and the closing beatitudes are later frame/application material.

paragraphs.core_text: the great Father of the [ligh]ts; since [a]ll [graces] are given by his hand.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed hagiographic/dialogue attribution and audience-address/application lead-in: “Once again the enlightener speaks: ‘Happen you know, my beloved ones, that [the beginn]ing of every good grace is …’” The “beginning of every good grace” formula functions as catechetical application (cosmos→human religious vocabulary).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Clear FRAME markers (“Once again…”, “my beloved ones”) plus a didactic ‘beginning of…’ schema. What can be earlier is the bare cosmological assertion of the Father of the Lights as source/giver.

paragraphs.core_text: the Mother of [L]ife, the first Holy Spirit.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the catechetical/application clause mapping to human religious acts: “The beginning of each blessing and every prayer is …”.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The ‘blessing/prayer’ side points outward to community piety, suggesting later catechesis; the divine title “Mother of Life” is core cosmological nomenclature, while “Holy Spirit” may reflect later Christianized terminology (uncertain).

paragraphs.core_text: the T[h/i]rd Am[bassad]or, the king of the glorious realm that lies in this [wo]rld, [ ... ] of the King of the lights.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the application/catechetical opener: “Also, [the] beginning [of] every good [co]unsel is …”.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Underlying content is purely hierarchical/cosmological identification (Third Ambassador; realm of glory), but the ‘beginning of every good counsel’ formula reads like a later pedagogical scaffold.

paragraphs.core_text: the Beloved of the Lights, who is honour[ed.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the ‘beginning of … honour’ catechetical frame: “The beginning of [ ... and] each [hono]ur (?) is …”.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Short titular identification likely preserves older list-material; the surrounding ‘beginning of…’ pattern maps into human valuation (“honour”), suggesting later catechetical shaping.

paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the outward-pointing category: “The beginning of a]ll [the trappers] and hunters is …”.
paragraphs.temporal_note: “First Man” is a core cosmological entity; “trappers and hunters” is an obvious cosmos→human-profession mapping, likely later application.

paragraphs.core_text: [the] Living [Spirit], the Father of Life, who has distribu[ted about] his five sons from place to place.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the remaining tail of the ‘beginning of…/of all fighters’ catechetical schema preceding the divine name: “... of] all fighters is …”. Also omitted the page marker.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The functional description (distribution of the five sons) is internal to the cosmic system and strongly marks older teaching; the ‘fighters’ label looks like a didactic hook aimed at human categories.

paragraphs.core_text: the Great Builder, who is glorious.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the mapping to human crafts: “The beginning of all the archit[e]cts and builders is …”.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Divine epithet “Great Builder” fits cosmological function-language, but the explicit appeal to “architects and builders” suggests a later explanatory bridge to everyday roles.

paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the catechetical lead-in tied to a human role-category: “Also, the first of all the porters of the gr[e]a[t]ness is …”.
paragraphs.temporal_note: “Pillar of Glory” is core cosmological vocabulary; the ‘porters’ framing looks like an application label grafted onto a list of Fathers of Light.

paragraphs.core_text: [Jesus the Splendour]; or the one who delivers, as he frees whoever belongs [ ... ] from his words.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the outward-pointing category phrase: “The beginning of [all] the deliverers [is …”.
paragraphs.temporal_note: “Jesus the Splendour” here functions as a named Manichaean cosmic being (not a Gospel citation), which can belong to the older teaching stratum; the ‘deliverers’ category is an explanatory human-facing label.

paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the catechetical opener: “The beginning of every wisdom of truth is …”.
paragraphs.temporal_note: “Virgin of Light” is core cosmological nomenclature; the ‘wisdom of truth’ framing suggests a later pedagogical assignment of abstract qualities to specific Fathers.

paragraphs.core_text: the Light Mind; who is the awakene[r of they] who sleep, the gatherer in of the ones who are sc[att]ered.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the ‘beginning of… honoured ones’ catechetical wrapper: “The beginning of] all [the great]est honoured ones [ ... ] is …”.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The functional descriptors (Awakener/Gatherer) are internal-cosmic roles and read like older substrate. The ‘honoured ones’ category again looks like a later explanatory heading.
Beatitude/exhortation aimed at the hearer (“Blessed is he… lodge this treasure… fasten… in his heart!”). This is application voice rather than impersonal cosmological exposition.
Continuation of beatitude and exhortation (“continue in their belief… inherit… eternal life”), functioning as pastoral application/closing rather than core system-description.
